gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-samarita: Unique from the first glance, Origami draws each stroke like one pass of a sign-painter's brush, at constant width. Noto Sans Samaritan, a plain sans with open curves, lets it breathe.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Heavy, brush-drawn lowercase at constant width: Origami looks poured from lead, with a y whose tail matches its arm. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri has an a whose lower bowl opens to breathe.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Constant-width strokes, poured-lead lowercase: Origami looks drawn with a compass pencil. Shrink Origami and its heavy lowercase loses punch, while Noto Sans Syriac Western, a sans-serif with far-flung terminals, keeps working.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Origami keeps full-width strokes right through its joins, like poured lead. Noto Sans Tagalog, a sans with a dominant middle zone and generous gaps in its curves, reads steadily over many lines.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Constant stroke width, like a ballpoint's pressure-free line, gives Origami a lowercase mass that looks poured from lead. Noto Sans Tagbanwa, a plain sans with open curves, reads smoothly across paragraphs.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-takri: Heavy, unbending brush lines: Origami never shifts weight along a curve. Noto Sans Takri, a sans with generously unclosed round letters, supplies the open counterpoint to those solid strokes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Contemporary through and through, Origami holds one stroke width everywhere. What stands out is Noto Sans Tamil, a plain sans that looks magnified at its ordinary size, its terminals stopping far from the stem.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tamil-su: Brush-drawn and bluntly uniform, Origami has a lowercase like poured lead. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement, a sans-serif with round forms like open parentheses and a tall middle band, reads stocky and steady line after line.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Blunt, steady, hard to knock off course: Origami skims along because its stroke weight never changes at all. Noto Sans Tangsa, a sans with wide round openings, keeps long reading inviting.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tc: Origami makes the loud first impression, its joins no thinner than its stems. Noto Sans TC, a sans-serif with outward-opening curves, is the one that carries the text.
